claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has improved plastic strain and toughness relative to commercially used pure tungsten.
Severe lattice distortion in the multi-element WTaTiVZr solid solution primarily governs the proposed improvement in plastic strain and toughness.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr produces a refined microstructure with stabilized sub-grain boundaries.
The stabilized sub-grain boundaries promote dynamic recovery and facilitate dislocation motion at high temperature.
The initial comparison is between fully recrystallized, homogenized equimolar WTaTiVZr and recrystallized commercial pure tungsten.
High-temperature tensile and fracture-toughness tests at approximately 1000–1200 °C under matched strain rates and controlled atmospheres can compare the two materials.
Temperatures around 1000–1200 °C are relevant to plasma-facing-component service.
W-containing WTaTiVZr has finer grain boundaries than recrystallized commercial pure tungsten under the proposed comparison.
WTaTiVZr contains a high density of stable dislocation substructures mediated by lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr hinders dislocation pile-up.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr accelerates dynamic recovery.
Microstructural refinement and dynamic recovery delay crack initiation and propagation during high-temperature deformation.
Pure tungsten has a coarser and less distortion-stabilized microstructure than WTaTiVZr.
Under identical high-temperature tests, WTaTiVZr will have greater plastic strain to failure than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature tests, WTaTiVZr will have greater fracture toughness than pure tungsten.
Post-deformation WTaTiVZr will show finer grains and lower dislocation density indicative of dynamic recovery relative to pure tungsten.
The proposed mechanistic advantage applies above approximately 1000 °C and may weaken at lower temperatures because dislocation activity and recovery differ.
Secondary-phase precipitation or grain-boundary segregation could modify the expected behavior of WTaTiVZr.
A lack of statistically significant improvement in both plastic strain and fracture toughness would falsify the proposed advantage.
Failure to observe the predicted finer grains or lower post-deformation dislocation density would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The mediator is described as a high density of stable dislocation substructures, whereas the predicted signature is lower post-deformation dislocation density. These can coexist if the former is an initial or transient state and the latter results from recovery, but that temporal distinction is not stated.
